Docket 1.3.94

**Four findings that tripped over how local businesses write their sites, and a title fix in the PDF.**

- *Topic suggestions built from a city name.* When you don't tell Docket what
  your site is about, it reads the subject off your titles — and for a local
  business the most repeated words are often the town. Each word was looked up
  on its own, so a site in a two-word city could be told to write about
  something that merely starts with one of them. A suggestion must now carry
  at least two of the words Docket read, and the finding says the subjects
  were read from your titles rather than given by you.
- *Phone numbers in code samples.* An article that shows a click-to-call link
  as sample code was listed as a page with an unclickable phone number. Code
  samples are now left out when Docket looks for your number.
- *An article about contact forms taken for the contact page.* "No map embed
  on the contact page" could name any page whose address merely contained the
  word "contact". A contact page is now one whose address is /contact,
  /contact-us and the like.
- *A price at the end of a title.* Pages built from one title pattern with
  one part changed are separate pages — but a price tag on the end ("from
  $999") hid that, and two services were reported as competing for one
  search. The price is now set aside before titles are compared.
- *The report's title in your PDF viewer.* The dash in "SEO & marketing audit —
  your business" showed as a stray "Š" in the viewer's title bar and the
  file's properties. The PDF's own title is now written so every reader shows
  it as typed.

99 checks across 13 areas.
